name: Production Distro RC6
source: TASK.md; RC5 final audit; maestro-managed continuation
goal: Turn the RC5 hosted metadata mirror into an installable signed payload channel and controlled canary execution readiness path while preserving signing, installer, activation, rollback, fleet, and TUI authority boundaries.
core_thesis: AIOS becomes Ubuntu-like only when users can inspect and consume signed, hash-bound payload metadata through a bootstrap/installer path; the hosted mirror remains transport, and all install, activation, rollback, signing, and canary execution authority stays with verified local clients, AgentCore, and SecurityExecutionEngine.
non_goals: Do not claim GA production readiness.
Do not store or read private production signing material on the mirror service.
Do not upload large release payloads to the limited mirror host until storage policy is defined and evidenced.
Do not allow nginx, static files, shell scripts, TUI, or model replay to install, activate, rollback, or mutate fleet rings.
Do not treat payload metadata reachability as payload trust without schema, hash, signature, revocation, freshness, and rollback verification.
primary_acceptance: The installable signed payload channel contract defines endpoint layout, payload metadata schema expectations, trust inputs, storage boundaries, and fail-closed behavior.
Bootstrap and installer consumption boundaries explain how a user can inspect AIOS payload metadata while install/activation remains blocked until signed payload and rollback evidence exist.
Hosted payload metadata is hash-bound to RC5 final audit and current release artifacts, but does not store large payloads in RC6 unless storage policy is upgraded.
Fail-closed fixtures reject unsigned, stale, revoked, oversized, hash-mismatched, or authority-broadening payload metadata.
Controlled canary execution remains exact-approval gated and rollback-ready; no production ring mutation is allowed by default.
